clue.text: Joke about girl that's a prude

indicators.note: one thing placed about another goes round it, so the joke wraps the girl

blocks.note: a pun is a joke on words
a girl's name

explanation.surface: Someone tells a smutty joke about a girl, and she disapproves.
explanation.definitionFit: A Puritan, by extension, is a person with strict and censorious moral views, which is what a prude has.

clue.text: Small foreign instrument

blocks.note: first meaning: the Italian word for little
second meaning: the small high-pitched flute

explanation.surface: Something like a tiny imported musical instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Foreign' tells you to translate 'small' rather than define it in English; the instrument is named after that very word.
explanation.definitionFit: Italian uses this word as the ordinary adjective for little, and English borrowed it for the half-size flute.

clue.text: Beast swallows another 500 and a large port

indicators.note: what an animal swallows ends up inside it, so the beast encloses the rest

blocks.note: a ram is a male sheep
another beast: an otter
D is the Roman numeral for 500

explanation.surface: A greedy animal gobbles up another animal and a large quantity besides.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Another' only makes sense as 'another beast', borrowing the noun from the first word.
explanation.definitionFit: The Dutch city at the mouth of the Rhine has long been one of the busiest seaports in Europe.

clue.text: Beat most of the swindle

indicators.note: most but not all of the word is used, so its final letter is dropped

blocks.note: taken as written, then cut short
to rob is to cheat or swindle

explanation.surface: Defeating the bulk of a con trick.
explanation.definitionFit: A heart's pulsing rhythm is a steady beat, so the noun and verb both match a regular pulse.

clue.text: Fruit makes a number react badly when eaten

indicators.note: react done badly is react done wrong, its letters put out of order
food that is eaten goes inside the eater, so the number holds the jumbled word

blocks.note: nine is a number
the letters of react, jumbled

explanation.surface: A piece of fruit makes several people come out in an allergic reaction after eating it.
explanation.definitionFit: A smooth-skinned variety of peach is a stone fruit eaten fresh in summer.

clue.text: Who the author mentioned in disbelief?

blocks.note: first meaning: a Victorian novelist, with 'Who the' echoing a startled question
second meaning: the mild oath in 'What the ...?', a euphemism for the devil

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about which writer someone is talking about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Who the author' echoes the exclamation 'What the ...?', where the blank is the novelist's surname, used as a mild oath.
explanation.definitionFit: The Victorian novelist's surname also serves as an old euphemism for the devil in exclamations of astonishment.

clue.text: End of novel 5 across never completed, so died cross

definitions.text: End of novel 5 across never completed

blocks.note: d. is the abbreviation for died
a rood is a crucifix

explanation.surface: A novelist died before finishing his book, and the reader is cross about it.
explanation.walkthrough: The Mystery of Edwin Drood was left unfinished when the author died in 1870, so its ending is unknown.
explanation.definitionFit: The surname of the title character ends the title of the last, unfinished novel by that writer.

clue.text: Mate given a ring, deliriously happy

blocks.note: cock is an old informal term of address for a friend, like mate
a hoop is a ring

explanation.surface: A friend who has just been handed an engagement ring is overjoyed.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes someone exultant and crowing with triumph, which is a delirious kind of joy.

clue.text: So be it! Point upwards to this treatment!

indicators.note: in a down entry going upwards means reading from the bottom, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: amen means 'so be it'
E is a compass point

explanation.surface: A grudging acceptance of an unpleasant medical procedure being pointed out.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry 'upwards' reads the letters from bottom to top.
explanation.definitionFit: Injecting fluid into the bowel is a medical procedure, a treatment for constipation.

clue.text: This Hugh, we're told, can be looked up to

definitions.text: This Hugh, we're told, can be looked up to

blocks.note: surface reading: a man called Hugh who is respected

blocks.clueFragment: we're told, can be looked up to
blocks.note: setter's reading: a colour (a sound-alike of the name) seen by gazing upward at the heavens

explanation.surface: A man named Hugh, it is said, is admirable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'We're told' turns Hugh into its sound-alike, a hue or colour; 'looked up to' is literal, since you look up to see it.
explanation.definitionFit: The pale colour of a clear daytime sky is a hue, and you must raise your eyes to see it.

clue.text: Provide for the 39th US President, not the 3rd

indicators.note: excluding the third letter of the president's surname, so that single letter is removed

blocks.note: Jimmy Carter was the 39th President

explanation.surface: Making provision for Jimmy Carter.
explanation.definitionFit: To supply food or whatever is needed for people is to look after their needs, as a caterer does.

clue.text: Irritable note unknown

blocks.note: a crotchet is a quarter note in music
y is an algebraic unknown

explanation.surface: A grumpy message from an anonymous sender.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone bad-tempered and easily annoyed is described as cranky or grumpy, the same as irritable.

clue.text: Running a company like Robert Maxwell?

definitions.note: describes how he went: fell from his yacht

blocks.note: first meaning: read as two words, in charge of the directors
second meaning: the press tycoon was lost from his yacht in 1991

explanation.surface: A question about running a business the way a notorious tycoon did.
explanation.walkthrough: Robert Maxwell, a British newspaper owner, died in 1991 after falling from his yacht; his businesses were then found to have looted pension funds.
explanation.definitionFit: Split in two the answer means above the directors, i.e. running things; whole, it means over the side of a ship into the sea.

clue.text: "I want a thousand giraffes on my desk by tomorrow morning"

definitions.text: "I want a thousand giraffes on my desk by tomorrow morning"

blocks.clueFragment: I want a thousand giraffes on my desk by tomorrow morning
blocks.note: surface reading: an absurd demand from a boss
setter's reading: the request is unreasonable, and also literally a request for lofty animals

explanation.surface: A boss makes a ridiculous overnight demand for a thousand giraffes.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase for an unreasonable demand is taken literally too: giraffes are the tallest animals, so ordering them is ordering something tall.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means a request that is very hard to fulfil, which the ridiculous demand plainly is.

clue.text: See 12
Take back knotted rope onto ships around the East

indicators.note: a rope that is knotted is twisted out of its straight line, so its letters get scrambled
the ships sit around the compass point, enclosing it on either side

blocks.note: the letters of rope, tied up differently
SS (steamship) twice, for the plural
E is the abbreviation for East

explanation.surface: Sailors recover a tangled rope and load it on vessels sailing round the Orient.
explanation.definitionFit: Creditors seize goods back when payments are missed, which is to recover ownership of them.

clue.text: Pound reduction to bring in

indicators.note: to pound something is to batter it out of shape, so the next word is rearranged

blocks.note: the fodder, every letter used

explanation.surface: A cut in the value of sterling is brought in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pound' looks like the currency, but it is the verb: to batter something into a new shape.
explanation.definitionFit: To present a new law or a person for the first time is to bring them in to a setting.

clue.text: Book of words based on the old reptile's tail

indicators.note: only the reptile's tail end is wanted, so the front part of its name is cut away

blocks.note: taken as written
a long-extinct dinosaur; only its end is kept

explanation.surface: A book whose text is based on a dinosaur's tail.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'tail' kept is the last six letters, the Greek ending meaning lizard shared by many dinosaur names.
explanation.definitionFit: A reference book listing synonyms and related terms is a lexicon grouping vocabulary by meaning.

clue.text: Finished my work, so hurtful

blocks.note: time's up means time has finished
the setter's work is setting puzzles

explanation.surface: A setter announces that the puzzle is done, and admits it may sting.
explanation.definitionFit: Something distressing or wounding to the feelings is the kind of remark that causes emotional pain.

clue.text: Watch me object after square one

blocks.note: a T-square, from its shape
I is the Roman numeral one
taken as written
a piece is an object or item

explanation.surface: An instruction to observe the speaker raising an objection after getting back to the start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Square one' wants to be the phrase meaning the beginning; it splits into two separate pieces. 'After' places the second pair behind the first.
explanation.definitionFit: A wristwatch is a portable clock, and both are devices for telling the time.

clue.text: Tiny boy grabs model, diamonds and the birds

indicators.note: the boy grabs and holds the model, so it sits inside his name

blocks.note: Tiny Tim, the crippled boy in A Christmas Carol
the Model T Ford
ice is slang for diamonds

explanation.surface: A small boy snatches a toy model and some jewels, along with some birds.
explanation.definitionFit: Tits are small songbirds; this is the old plural of the name, a set of such birds.

clue.text: After one Latin meal ...

blocks.note: past means after, as in past ten o'clock
a means one

explanation.surface: After eating one Italian dinner, the speaker trails off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Latin' here means from a Latin country, Italy, not the ancient language.
explanation.definitionFit: Spaghetti and other dough dishes are the staple food of Italy, a Latin nation.

clue.text: Bloomer getting confused on 7

indicators.note: letters that get confused become muddled, ending up in a different order

blocks.note: taken as written
the answer to 7 down

explanation.surface: A mistake made while confused about a medical treatment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bloomer' looks like a blunder, but it is something that blooms.
explanation.definitionFit: The windflower is a plant that produces blossoms, so it is a flowering thing, something that blooms.

clue.text: ... or maybe another?

indicators.note: 'or maybe' suggests an alternative version of the same letters, a possible rearrangement

blocks.note: the ellipsis carries over the answer to the previous clue, 19 across

explanation.walkthrough: The dots join this clue to 19 across: 'another' is another meal, and the letters of that answer rearrange to give it.
explanation.definitionFit: Small Spanish savoury dishes served with drinks make up a meal, so they are another kind of eating.

clue.text: Money, a pound given to the church

blocks.note: a pound for animals is a pen or enclosure
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: Cash, a pound coin, donated to the church collection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pound' looks like the coin; it is the animal enclosure.
explanation.definitionFit: Small British coins, a hundred to the pound, are units of cash.

clue.text: Girl that's sweet etc comes back to embrace one that's not

definitions.note: both a girl's name and a pudding

indicators.note: something that comes back travels in the opposite direction, so the abbreviation is read backwards
to embrace is to put one's arms around, so the reversed letters enclose the other piece

blocks.note: the letters of etc
one that's not sweet and innocent: a prostitute

explanation.surface: A sweet girl returns to hug someone who is anything but.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One that's not' leans on the definition: someone who is not a nice girl.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is a girl's name and also a baked dessert of fruit in sponge or bread.

clue.text: A restricted chicken?

blocks.note: surface reading: a hen kept in a cage or run
setter's reading: with a limit placed on it, i.e. a castrated cockerel whose sex life has been capped

explanation.surface: A battery hen kept in confinement.
explanation.walkthrough: Split in two, the answer reads 'cap on', a restriction; whole, it is a castrated cockerel fattened for eating.
explanation.definitionFit: A cockerel that has been castrated has its manhood curtailed, a bird with a limit on it.

clue.text: Cricketer is about five, so form not yet developed

indicators.note: the cricketer is placed about the numeral, surrounding it on both sides

blocks.note: Brian Lara, the West Indies batsman
V is the Roman numeral for five

explanation.surface: A batsman is only about five years old, so his technique is still raw.
explanation.walkthrough: Brian Lara was a star West Indian cricketer, famous in 1999.
explanation.definitionFit: A grub or caterpillar is an insect in its immature stage, before it becomes an adult.

clue.text: Landlord's rent offered during meal, though without starter

indicators.note: the rent is paid during the meal, so it falls in the middle of it
a meal without its starter loses the first course, so the opening letter goes

blocks.note: dinner is a meal, here losing its first letter
keep is money paid for board and lodging

explanation.surface: A landlord collects his rent at dinner but skips the first course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Starter' looks like the first course of the meal; it is the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The proprietor of a pub or hotel is its landlord, running the house and taking guests' money.

clue.text: One-horn creation

indicators.note: a creation is something made up from raw material, here the letters reshaped

blocks.note: I is the Roman numeral one
taken as written

explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: the Indian species of this animal has a single horn.
explanation.definitionFit: The Indian species is a large hoofed animal that bears one horn on its snout, a creature built around it.

clue.text: American writer making men sore

indicators.note: making the answer out of the following words means building it from their rearranged letters

blocks.note: the fodder, all seven letters

explanation.surface: An American author whose work irritates men.
explanation.definitionFit: Ralph Waldo Emerson was the nineteenth-century New England essayist and poet of Transcendentalism.

clue.text: Odds on fish will provide glitter

blocks.note: SP is the starting price, the odds at a race's start
to angle is to fish

explanation.surface: Betting on fishing promises something dazzling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On' just places one piece before the other.
explanation.definitionFit: A small shiny disc sewn on clothes gives sparkle, so as a verb or noun it means sparkling decoration.
